summary: Sustained 5xxs after route weight change: tainted prefetch cache + priority-queue starvation
description: Issue summary: After a customer-directed route weight adjustment this morning, Atlas reported a sustained rise in 5xx responses from the API (primarily 502/503). Impact: ~18% of requests for the tenant returned 5xx over a 22-minute window, causing user-facing failures in chat and embedding uploads. Environment: Dedicated tenant in prod (us-east) using pinned instances and prefetch enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Apply route weight change (route weight shifted from default pool -> new pool) 2) Resume normal traffic ramp for tenant 3) Observe elevated 5xxs and increased runtime restart counts Observed behavior: API gateway returns 502/503; serving runtimes show repeated model-prefetch evictions and KV cache miss storms. Runtime logs contain frequent "prefetch-lock-timeout" and "connection lease expired" messages. Expected behavior: Route weight change should redirect traffic without increasing 5xx floor; prefetch cache eviction should be graceful without triggering runtime crash/restarts. Initial hypothesis: Misrouted traffic landed on a small set of warm runtimes while a prefetch-eviction race left those runtimes with tainted kvcache states; combined with ingress prioritizer dropping lower-priority requests, this led to priority-queue starvation and upstream connection churn causing 5xx amplification.
investigation_notes: 13:02 UTC - Alert: tenant Atlas saw error-rate jump from baseline 0.6% -> 18%. Notified via #support and #incidents.
13:05 UTC - api-gateway metrics show surge in upstream 502s; 95th latency for successful requests increased from 220ms -> 1.4s.
13:08 UTC - serving-runtime team observed repeated "prefetch-lock-timeout" and kvcache eviction spikes on three nodes (node ids: s-ea-12, s-ea-15, s-ea-23).
13:12 UTC - ingress prioritizer logs show several priority-shed events for tenant traffic coincident with route weight change (link: slack://channel#incidents/clip-xyz).
13:18 UTC - Identified that connection leases to the runtime pool expired aggressively due to a stale client keepalive policy during the traffic handoff.

13:24 UTC - Correlated runtime restarts with a prefetch eviction bug where tainted entries triggered heavy KV lock contention (see runtime PR attempt: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4582).
comments: Support (Ethan Myers) 13:10: Thanks for reporting, Atlas. We're triaging — can you confirm if you changed route weights or did this via the Console rollouts?
Customer (Atlas SRE - Maria Lopez) 13:11: We applied a 60/40 weight shift to a new pool at 12:58 UTC as part of a planned capacity migration. We saw errors within ~4 minutes.

Support (Priya Shah) 13:16: Noted. Engineering is looking at prefetch/kvcache metrics and ingress prioritizer traces. Posting initial investigation in #incidents: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/CINC12345/p164...

Eng (Jin Park) 13:22: Found repeated "kvcache:taint_detected" events on s-ea-15; runtime restarted after OOM fragmentation on driver. Hypothesis: eviction race left kvcache locks held causing downstream timeouts.

Eng (Priya Shah) 13:30: Applied short-term mitigation: temporarily pinned Atlas route to previous pool, increased connection lease TTL on the client side, and invalidated prefetch index for the tenant. Error rate dropped to 1.7% within 6 minutes.
Customer (Maria Lopez) 13:37: Confirmed traffic recovery and reduced user errors. Requesting postmortem and long-term fixes.

Support (Priya Shah) 13:55: Creating follow-ups: (1) fix eviction race in runtime (PR linked), (2) add graceful prefetch invalidation on route changes, (3) add ingress prioritizer backoff on rapid weight changes.
resolution: Workaround applied: rolled back route weight to original pool, increased client connection lease TTL, and issued a tenant-specific prefetch invalidation which reduced the 5xx rate to baseline. Permanent remediation planned: runtime patch to prevent tainted-kv eviction races (PR opened), change Console rollout to perform staged weight shifts with ingress backoff, and add a runtime-side guard to refuse prefetch invalidation storms. Postmortem scheduled and runbook updated.
resolution_notes: Short-term: rollback weight + prefetch invalidate (13:30 UTC) — immediate decrease in 5xxs.
Medium-term: runtime PR to serialize prefetch evictions and avoid taint (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4582) — targeted deploy 2026-03-18.
Long-term: Console change to staged rollouts with minimum grace window and ingress prioritizer smoothing to prevent priority starvation during pool transitions.
Follow-up action: update dedicated-customer runbook for weight shifts and add automated tenant prefetch drain on route changes.
